title: Advice that stops at the doorstep
odia: କହି ଦେଉଥାଇ ପରକୁ, ବୁଦ୍ଧି ନ ଦିଶଇ ଘରକୁ
literal_meaning: One keeps advising others, but wisdom is not seen at home.
explanation: The criticism is the gap between giving advice and practising it. The outward-facing adviser appears wise, yet fails to apply that wisdom to their own affairs. The saying invites self-examination; it does not imply that advice is worthless whenever its giver has difficulties.
meaning_odia: ଅନ୍ୟକୁ ଭଲ ପରାମର୍ଶ ଦେବା ସହଜ, ନିଜ ଜୀବନରେ ସେହି କଥା ମାନିବା କଷ୍ଟକର ହୋଇପାରେ। ଉପଦେଶ ଓ ନିଜ ଆଚରଣ ମଧ୍ୟର ଏହି ଫାଙ୍କକୁ କଥାଟି ଟିପ୍ପଣୀ କରେ। କହୁଥିବା ଲୋକ ନିଜେ ଭୁଲ୍ କରନ୍ତି ବୋଲି ପରାମର୍ଶଟି ଅବଶ୍ୟ ଭୁଲ୍ ହେବ, ଏମିତି ନୁହେଁ।
usage_example: A person lectures everyone about keeping accounts but repeatedly loses track of their own spending. A relative uses this line to point out the inconsistency. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: The rhyme of ପରକୁ and ଘରକୁ reinforces the contrast between others and home. Here the structure is part of the saying’s force, not just decoration.

title: Naming the child before the family exists
odia: ମୁଳୁରୁ ମାଇପ ନାହିଁ ପୁଅ ନାଁ ଗୋପାଳ
literal_meaning: There is no wife to begin with, yet the son is named Gopal.
explanation: Plans have moved ahead of the conditions needed to carry them out. The family scene makes the missing first step conspicuous: a later detail has been settled while the basic situation is still imaginary. It can mock premature certainty rather than planning itself.
meaning_odia: ମୂଳ ଆୟୋଜନ ହୋଇନାହିଁ, ଅଥଚ ବହୁତ ପରର କଥାର ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତି ସରିଲାଣି। ପୁଅର ନାଁ ଠିକ୍ କରିବାର ଚିତ୍ରରେ ଏହି ଅକାଳ ନିଶ୍ଚିତତାକୁ ହସି କୁହାଯାଇଛି। କାମର ପ୍ରଥମ ଶର୍ତ୍ତଟି ପୂରଣ ହେବା ଆଗରୁ ଶେଷ ଫଳକୁ ନିଜର ବୋଲି ଧରିନେବା ହିଁ ଏଠାରେ ମୁଖ୍ୟ।
usage_example: A club chooses the colour of its new building before securing any place to build it. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: The wording uses a blunt term for wife and a familiar personal name. It documents a domestic image, not a rule about marriage, parenthood or a person’s entitlement to either.

title: A straw-bundle adviser
literal_meaning: For an uncomprehending king, a bundle-of-straw minister.
explanation: Poor leadership is compounded by equally foolish advice. The pairing, rather than the ruler alone, is the target.
meaning_odia: ନେତୃତ୍ୱରେ ବିଚାରର ଅଭାବ, ପରାମର୍ଶରେ ବି ସାର ନାହିଁ—ଦୁଇଟି ଦୁର୍ବଳତା ଏକାଠି ହୋଇଛି। ସୁବିଚାରପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ପରାମର୍ଶର ଅଭାବରୁ ଭୁଲ୍ ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତି ଆହୁରି ବିଗିଡ଼ୁଥିବା ଅବସ୍ଥାକୁ କଥାଟି ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ କରେ। ପଦବୀ ଥିବା ଓ ସେହି ପଦର କାମ ଠିକ୍ ଭାବେ କରିବା ଅଲଗା କଥା।
usage_example: An ill-planned proposal survives because the person asked to assess it understands it no better. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: Straw-bundle is a belittling image. The source gloss explicitly describes a foolish adviser to an unjust ruler.

title: Say what you want in time
odia: ଚଇତା ! ତବତ ଖାଇବୁ କି ପଖାଳ ଖାଇବୁ ବେଳ ଥାଉଁ ଥାଉଁ କହିଥା
literal_meaning: Chaita! Will you eat hot food or pakhala? Say so while there is still time.
explanation: The pointed address and choice between hot food and pakhala turn a practical request into a memorable line: say what you want while another person still has time to arrange it. The dictionary marks Chaita as a non-respectful form of Chaitanya, so the tone can carry impatience or a dismissive edge. Applying it to other decisions is an editorial reading of the complete quoted example; its first occasion is unknown.
meaning_odia: ତବତ ଖାଦ୍ୟ ନା ପଖାଳ—କଣ ଖାଇବ, ତାହା ବେଳ ଥାଉଁ କହିବାକୁ ଚଇତାକୁ କୁହାଯାଉଛି। ଅନ୍ୟ ଜଣେ ବ୍ୟବସ୍ଥା କରିବାକୁ ହେଲେ ଆମ ଇଚ୍ଛାଟି ଆଗରୁ ଜାଣିବା ଦରକାର। ସବୁ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତି ସରିଗଲା ପରେ ମତ ବଦଳାଇବାଠାରୁ ସମୟରେ କହିଦେବା ଭଲ—ଏହି ଦୈନନ୍ଦିନ ବିଚାରଟି ଏଠି ଖାଇବା କଥାରେ ଆସିଛି।
english_summary: A meal cannot be arranged around an answer that arrives too late.
odia_summary: ତବତ ଖାଦ୍ୟ ନା ପଖାଳ—କଣ ଖାଇବ, ତାହା ବେଳ ଥାଉଁ କହିବାକୁ ଚଇତାକୁ କୁହାଯାଉଛି।
usage_example: A friend arranging a shared journey asks everyone to confirm their plans before tickets are booked. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: The source identifies Chaita as a non-respectful or dismissive form of Chaitanya. No particular historical person or household is established. Pakhala remains a named food; the wording should not be softened into a uniformly polite request.

odia: ପରଧନେ ଲହର ଫହର; ଛଡାଇ ନେଲେ ଲାଜେ ମର
title: A flourish on someone else’s wealth
literal_meaning: You move about in style on another’s wealth; when it is taken away, you die of shame.
explanation: The first half gives someone room to move and make a show; the second suddenly takes that support away. The dictionary defines the headword as moving to and fro, while the verse puts that movement on another person’s wealth. Read as a taunt, it catches the embarrassment of displaying what one cannot claim as one’s own. The closing “die of shame” is exaggerated reproach, not a literal instruction. Our wider reading concerns borrowed display and insecure pretension, not the worth of people who receive help.
meaning_odia: ପରର ଧନରେ ଚାଲିଛି ଲହର ଫହର; ସେ ଧନ ଫେରିଗଲେ ଦେଖାଣିର ଭିତ୍ତିଟି ମଧ୍ୟ ରହେନାହିଁ। ପ୍ରଥମ ଭାଗର ଆରାମ ଓ ଚଳପ୍ରଚଳକୁ ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଭାଗର ଲାଜ ହଠାତ୍ ଅଟକାଇଦିଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ନିଜର ନୁହେଁ ଏମିତି ଜିନିଷକୁ ନିଜ ବଡ଼ପଣର ପ୍ରମାଣ କରି ଦେଖାଇବା ଏହି ଟାହିର ଲକ୍ଷ୍ୟ। “ଲାଜେ ମର” କଥାର ଅତିରଞ୍ଜନ; ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ନେଉଥିବା ମଣିଷକୁ ଛୋଟ କରିବା ଏଠାରେ ଆମର ପଢ଼ା ନୁହେଁ।
english_summary: Borrowed display can become embarrassment when its support is withdrawn.
odia_summary: ପରର ଧନରେ ନିଜ ବଡ଼ପଣ ଦେଖାଇଲେ, ତାହା ଫେରିଗଲେ ଲାଜରେ ପଡ଼ିବାର ଟାହି।
usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone poses with a friend’s expensive camera and lets others think it belongs to them. When the friend asks for it back, another friend quotes the saying softly. The joke concerns the false impression, not borrowing a camera.
cultural_context: The dictionary labels the headword Sambalpur; this is a source label, not proof of exclusive regional origin. The display reading is editorial close reading, not an independently supplied traditional-use gloss.

title: Start again for the headman
literal_meaning: When the headman arrives, sing from the beginning.
explanation: In our reading, a late arrival changes where the song must begin. Placed under “village headman,” the line brings authority into that restart. Our reading hears a teasing complaint: everyone else has already listened, but the important newcomer gets the beginning again. The dictionary supplies the role, not a documented performance custom or this modern meeting application.
meaning_odia: ଆସିଥିବା ଲୋକଟି ପାଇଁ ଗୀତ ପୁଣି ମୂଳରୁ ଆରମ୍ଭ ହୁଏ। ଅଭିଧାନର ଗ୍ରାମପ୍ରଧାନ ଅର୍ଥ ଏହି ପୁନରାରମ୍ଭରେ ପଦମର୍ଯ୍ୟାଦାକୁ ଆଣେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଟିକେ ଟାହି ଅଛି—ଅନ୍ୟମାନେ ଶୁଣିସାରିଲେଣି, ତଥାପି ବଡ଼ଲୋକଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ପୁଣି ଆରମ୍ଭ! ଅଭିଧାନ ଭୂମିକାଟି ବୁଝାଏ; କୌଣସି ପ୍ରମାଣିତ ଗାୟନପ୍ରଥା ବା ଆଜିର ସଭାର ଉଦାହରଣ ଦିଏନାହିଁ।
english_summary: Our reading hears a teasing restart for someone with authority.
odia_summary: ପଦମର୍ଯ୍ୟାଦା ପାଇଁ ପୁଣି ଆରମ୍ଭ କରିବାର ଟାହି।
usage_example: Original imagined example: The chairperson joins after a club discussion has nearly finished and asks for the opening explanation again. A member quietly quotes the line to a neighbour, then offers a short recap. This is an invented application, not a recorded village practice.
cultural_context: The quotation belongs to the village-headman sense, separately from the headword’s family-title and military senses. It identifies no present caste, family or officeholder.

odia: ଛୋଟ ମୁହଁରେ ବଡ଼ କଥା, ଶୁଣିଲା ଲୋକର ମନ ବ୍ୟଥା
title: Whose words cause offence?
literal_meaning: Big words from a small mouth: the listener’s mind is hurt.
explanation: The dictionary’s “small” marks a person treated as low or insignificant. The line places the listener’s hurt beside that person’s speech. Our critical reading asks whether the offence comes from the words or from refusing the speaker standing. That question challenges the hierarchy; it is not a tolerant moral supplied by the saying.
meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନରେ “ଛୋଟ” କଥାଟି ନୀଚ ବା ନଗଣ୍ୟ ବୋଲି ଧରାଯାଇଥିବା ମଣିଷକୁ ସୂଚାଏ। ସେ ମଣିଷର କଥା ପାଖରେ ଶ୍ରୋତାର ମନବ୍ୟଥା ରଖାଯାଇଛି। ଆମର ସମାଲୋଚନାତ୍ମକ ପଢ଼ାରେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ—କଥାଟି ବାଧିଲା, ନା କହୁଥିବା ଲୋକକୁ ମର୍ଯ୍ୟାଦା ଦେବାର ଅନିଚ୍ଛା? ଏହି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଉଚ୍ଚନୀଚ ବିଚାର ଉପରେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଉଠାଏ; ଢଗଟି ନିଜେ ସହନଶୀଳତାର ନୀତି ଶିଖାଉଛି ବୋଲି କୁହାଯାଉନାହିଁ।
english_summary: Our critical reading separates a speaker’s standing from the worth of the words.
odia_summary: ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାତ୍ମକ ପଢ଼ାରେ ବକ୍ତାର ସ୍ଥାନ ଓ କଥାର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ଅଲଗା।
usage_example: Original imagined example: ନୂଆ ସଦସ୍ୟ ହିସାବର ଏକ ଭୁଲ ଦେଖାଇଲେ। ଜଣେ ଢଗଟି କହି ତାଙ୍କୁ ଚୁପ୍ କରାଇବାକୁ ଚାହିଁଲେ। ସଭାପତି କହିଲେ, “ସେ କେତେଦିନର ସଦସ୍ୟ, ତାହା ନୁହେଁ; ହିସାବଟି ମେଳୁଛି କି ଦେଖିବା।” / A newcomer points out an accounting error. Someone invokes the saying to silence them. The chair replies, “Their membership is recent; let us still check the figures.” This critical exchange is invented.
cultural_context: Historical rank language is retained as source evidence, not a judgment of anyone’s worth. The source identifies no caste, age, gender or particular speaker in the quotation.

title: Borrowing and answering for another
literal_meaning: I would borrow, but would not become surety for someone else.
explanation: The dictionary’s inline explanation distinguishes taking a loan from guaranteeing another person. The first-person voice accepts one involvement and refuses the other. Our reading hears a boundary between bearing one’s own obligation and answering for someone else; it does not turn that preference into a rule everyone should follow.
meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନର ସଂଲଗ୍ନ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଋଣ ନେବା ଓ ଅନ୍ୟ ପାଇଁ ଜାମିନ ହେବାକୁ ଅଲଗା କରେ। ବକ୍ତା ଗୋଟିଏ ସମ୍ପର୍କରେ ପଶିବାକୁ ମାନେ, ଅନ୍ୟଟିକୁ ମନା କରେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ନିଜ ଦାୟ ନେବା ଓ ପର ପାଇଁ ଉତ୍ତରଦାୟୀ ହେବା ମଧ୍ୟରେ ସୀମା ଶୁଣାଯାଏ; ସେ ପସନ୍ଦ ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ନିୟମ ହୋଇଯାଏନାହିଁ।
english_summary: Our reading hears a speaker distinguishing two kinds of obligation.
odia_summary: ଦୁଇ ପ୍ରକାର ଦାୟକୁ ଅଲଗା କରୁଥିବା ବକ୍ତାକୁ ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ଶୁଣେ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: ପାଠଚକ୍ରରେ ଜଣେ କହିଲେ, “କଥାଟିରେ ଋଣଠାରୁ ଅଧିକ ଦାୟର ଭେଦ ମୋତେ ଶୁଣାଯାଉଛି।” ଅନ୍ୟଜଣ ପଚାରିଲେ, “ନିଜ ପାଇଁ କହିବା ଓ ପର ପାଇଁ କଥା ଦେବା କି ଏକା?” / A reading group discusses the difference between speaking for oneself and giving one’s word for someone else. This discussion is invented, not borrowing advice.
cultural_context: Sambalpur labels the dictionary’s verb, not a proven saying origin. The gloss supplies surety; this historical wording offers no present financial or legal guidance.
